subject: Inference economics brief + budget escrow options
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-15T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Inference economics brief + budget escrow options

Hi Chloe / BlueAnchor team —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call + where we left off on cost and next steps so we have a single place to track decisions. I captured the high‑level constraints and a pragmatic pilot we think will prove value while staying within your budget gating.

Call highlights / confirmed pain points
- Avg. latency SLO: 100–150ms for authorization flows (90th pct).
- Volume profile: ~25M auth transactions/mo, but only ~10–15% will hit the LLM path initially (~2.5–3.75M calls/mo).
- Token characteristics: typical prompt ~120 tokens, response ~90 tokens (avg 210 tokens per round trip).
- Budget constraints: initial procurement commit is a hard cap of $45k/mo for inference spend during pilot.
- Risk concerns: data residency + audit logs and predictable unit economics.

Cost framing & levers we discussed
- Baseline hosted price run: with model X at current throughput, expected spend ~ $60–70k/mo for full 3.5M calls (no batching).
- Batching & caching levers: applying small per‑client batching windows (20–50ms) and prefix KV caching for repeated auth prompts reduces token volume ~30–40% on our estimates.
- Quantization & model variant routing: routing lower‑sensitivity traffic to a quantized variant can cut per‑token compute cost by another ~25%.
- Net practical outcome: combined levers reduce expected spend into the $36–45k/mo band depending on hit rates (this puts pilot within your stated cap).

Proposed pilot structure (two‑phase, 6 weeks)
1) Week 0–2: Pilot staging — metrics baseline, set up routing policies, enable prefix KV cache for top 10 client patterns.
2) Week 3–6: Production canary — scale to representative subset (~10% of auth traffic) and measure real savings.

Key asks from BlueAnchor (what we need to unblock)
- Confirmation that procurement can commit up to $45k/mo for the pilot window.
- Two anonymized sample auth flows and one representative prompt set for cache tuning.
- Access to a staging environment with mirrored traffic (or allow Redwood to accept a 10% traffic mirror for the canary).

Deliverables from Redwood
- Pilot scope doc + cost sensitivity sheet (attached).
- Weekly SLO & spend snapshots; post‑pilot ROI brief with projected steady‑state spend at scale.

Attachments
- [Attachment: redwood_econ-one-pager.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
- [Attachment: pilot-scope-template.xlsx (Excel, 35KB)]

Next steps
- Chloe: confirm budget gating + who on procurement we should loop for doc review (Procurement email copied).
- BlueAnchor: send the sample prompts / staging access details.
- Redwood (Marissa/Ben): we’ll prepare a short config playbook and a canary runbook.

I’ll circle back with a formal pilot scope doc by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Diego —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from our side:
- Procurement can provision up to $45k/mo for the 6‑week pilot but needs an itemized run rate and a 30‑day termination clause.
- We’ll provide two redacted auth flows and a CSV of top 250 prompts by frequency by Friday.
- Staging: we can mirror traffic to a vendor endpoint; I’ll share the ingress details with Marissa.

Two clarifying questions:
1) On routing to the quantized variant: what QA metrics do you need to ensure there isn’t a regression in authorization accuracy?
2) If caching yields 35% fewer tokens, do you have a simple sensitivity table showing spend at 20/35/50% savings? That will help procurement model the risk.

We’re broadly aligned — next, procurement wants to see the itemized pilot pricing and a short demonstration of the caching behavior (even a recorded session is fine).

Thanks,
Chloe Tan
Head of Product Integrations | BlueAnchor Payments

> - We’ll provide two redacted auth flows and a CSV of top 250 prompts by frequency by Friday.

> 2) If caching yields 35% fewer tokens, do you have a simple sensitivity table showing spend at 20/35/50% savings? That will help procurement model the risk.

Thanks — short answers below and we’ll attach the detailed sensitivity table in the pilot scope doc.

1) QA / acceptance for quantized variant
- Primary metric: authorization decision parity (match rate) vs baseline classifier >= 99.5% on sampled auth flows.
- Secondary: end‑to‑end latency delta (p95) must be within +25ms of baseline on quantized path.
- We’ll run an A/B sample of 5k flows to validate parity prior to routing any production traffic.

2) Sensitivity table (excerpt) — assumed baseline cost (no levers) $0.020 per full request compute token cost; full monthly traffic 3.5M calls, avg 210 tokens/request
- No levers: ~ $63,000/month
- 20% token savings: ~ $50,400/month
- 35% token savings: ~ $40,950/month
- 50% token savings: ~ $31,500/month

I’ll attach the full spreadsheet in the pilot scope doc (we’ll include alternate routes: model variant routing %, cache hit rate sensitivity, and a recommended default config that hits ~35% savings in early runs).

Action items / next steps
- Diego: deliver pilot scope + itemized run rate by EOD tomorrow (attaching one‑pager and the spreadsheet).
- BlueAnchor: send redacted flows + staging ingress by Friday.
- Procurement: if you can share standard PO/contract language, we’ll confirm termination clause timing.

Thanks —
Diego
